Buying Off-Plan Property in Phuket

Pre-sale and under-construction projects: benefits, risks and checks
HomeGuidesBuying Off-Plan Property in Phuket

Buying property · Last reviewed: 2026-11-23

Off-plan means you buy a unit before the building is finished. Many new Phuket projects are sold this way. It can give access to a lower entry price and a choice of units, and it also carries construction and delay risk. This guide explains how it works and what to verify.

What counts as off-plan in our catalogue

Projects marked Pre-sale have launched sales before or at the start of construction. Under construction projects are being built. Completed projects are finished and can be viewed. At the moment 52 of our 90 catalogue projects are pre-sale or under construction, and 27 are completed.

How payment normally works

A typical structure is a booking fee, a deposit when you sign the sale and purchase agreement and then instalments tied to construction stages, with a final payment at completion and transfer. Our standard reference is a THB 100,000 booking fee, 20% on contract signing and the remaining 80% in construction-linked instalments, but every developer sets its own plan. We show a developer’s own plan on the project page when we have it.

Advantages and risks, side by side

  • Advantage: wider unit choice and often a lower entry price than a finished comparable unit.
  • Advantage: payments are spread over the build period.
  • Risk: delays. The completion date shown is the developer’s advertised target, not a guarantee.
  • Risk: the finished building may differ from renders and show-unit photos.
  • Risk: you hold a contract, not yet a title, until transfer.
  • Risk: developer financial strength matters more when you pay before you can see the product.

What to check before you reserve

  • Developer history: completed projects and how they performed against their dates.
  • Land title and building permits for this project, checked by your lawyer.
  • Contract clauses: delay compensation, termination and refund, what happens to your deposit.
  • Payment protection: ask how construction-linked payments are tied to verified progress.
  • Foreign quota availability for the unit you want.
  • Specification list: finishes, furniture, parking, facilities and when they will open.

Visiting and monitoring

Ask for dated construction photos and, if you are abroad, periodic site updates. Compare them with the schedule in the contract.

Off-plan or completed?

If you want certainty about what you buy and a fast handover, a completed unit is simpler. If you want a lower entry price and can accept the wait, off-plan can fit. Both are available in our catalogue; you can filter by construction status in Sale and New Projects.

Frequently asked questions

Is the completion date guaranteed?

No. It is the developer’s target. Your contract should state delay remedies.

Can I resell before completion?

Some contracts allow assigning your rights, some restrict it, and developers may charge a fee. Check the contract and ask your lawyer.

Are the photos on project pages real?

Many are developer renders for projects not yet built. Where we know images are renders, the project page says so.
